name: php-moves-before-the-typo3-major
prompt: We are on TYPO3 12.4 with PHP 8.1 and want to reach 13.4 with PHP 8.4. In which order should we move, and why that order?

assertions.description: Raises PHP before the TYPO3 major rather than in the same step
Names 8.4 as already reachable on the current 12.4, so the PHP step needs no TYPO3 change
Gives the reason: a failure then has one candidate cause instead of two
Names the class of failure the PHP step surfaces on its own

samples.passing: Raise PHP first: 12.4 already supports 8.4, so move to 8.4 on 12.4, test there and fix the PHP-level failures — undefined array keys above all — and only then upgrade TYPO3 to 13.4. That isolates 'is this PHP or TYPO3?' while debugging instead of leaving both variables in play.
failing: Upgrade TYPO3 to 13.4 first and raise PHP afterwards; 13.4 supports 8.2, so the old PHP is fine during the upgrade.
Do both in one deployment to save a release cycle.

name: php-support-bounds-per-lts
prompt: Which PHP versions do TYPO3 13.4 and 14.3 support, and does a 13.4 to 14.3 upgrade force a PHP move?

assertions.description: Names 8.2 as the minimum for both
Names 8.5 as the current upper bound for both
States that the two ranges coincide, so the TYPO3 step does not force a PHP step

samples.passing: Both support 8.2 through 8.5. The ranges coincide, so a 13.4 to 14.3 upgrade needs no PHP move — take 8.5 as a separate step afterwards if you want it.
failing: 13.4 supports 8.2 to 8.4 and 14.3 requires at least 8.3, so you have to raise PHP as part of the upgrade.
TYPO3 14 requires PHP 8.5, so plan the PHP upgrade first.

name: core-extensions-cost-zero-hours
prompt: Our composer.json lists 31 typo3/cms-* packages plus 12 third-party extensions. How many of the 43 do I put hours on for a v14 upgrade?

assertions.description: Prices the core packages at zero hours instead of per-package
Estimates only the 12 third-party extensions
Explains why: core packages move with the core release itself

samples.passing: Only the 12 third-party ones. The 31 typo3/cms-* packages are classified LOW / 0 h — they move with the core release, so they are a composer constraint bump and nothing else.
failing: All 43 need to be assessed individually; budget a couple of hours each, so roughly 90 hours for the extension work.
Core extensions are the riskiest part of a major upgrade — estimate them first.

name: magic-finder-trigger-is-a-call-site-not-a-method-name
prompt: I grepped an extension for findBy and got 14 hits. Its repository defines findByCategory() itself using createQuery(). Does the magic-finder multiplier apply, and how should I have decided?

assertions.description: Does not apply the multiplier to a self-defined repository method
Ties the multiplier to Extbase's __call magic finders, which is what v14 removed
Distinguishes a call site relying on __call from a method the repository declares itself
Names the multiplier that would apply if the trigger did match

samples.passing: No. The x1.1 factor covers Extbase's __call magic finders, which v14.0 removed. A repository method the class declares itself and implements with createQuery() is ordinary code and unaffected, so 14 grep hits on the name prove nothing — the trigger is a call site that relies on __call, which means checking whether the method exists before counting it.
failing: Yes, 14 findBy hits means the magic-finder multiplier applies; use x1.1.
Grep for findBy and multiply by 1.1 per extension that has any hit; Rector fixes them anyway.
